body_text: View All News THE REALREAL ANNOUNCES SECOND QUARTER 2026 RESULTS August 6, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Company Raises Full Year Guidance Following Second Quarter Results Above the High End of Outlook with Record Quarterly GMV and Meaningful Margin Expansion SAN FRANCISCO , Aug. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The RealReal, Inc. (Nasdaq: REAL)—the world's largest online marketplace for authenticated, resale luxury goods—today reported financial results for its second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Second quarter 2026 gross merchandise value (GMV) and total revenue increased 22% and 17% compared to the second quarter of 2025, respectively. Consignment revenue grew 15% compared to the prior year period, and Direct Revenue grew 26% year-over-year in the second quarter. During the quarter, gross margin of 74.4% improved 10 basis points compared to the same period in 2025. Second quarter Adjusted EBITDA margin was 7.0%, an increase of 290 basis points versus the prior year period. "The RealReal delivered a standout second quarter, with an all-time high quarterly GMV of $617 million, up 22% year-over-year. That marks our fourth consecutive quarter of GMV growth above 20%. Revenue grew 17% and we delivered nearly 300 basis points of Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion versus last year," said Rati Levesque, Chief Executive Officer of The RealReal. "We're upleveling the customer experience, deepening trust and compounding our advantages. Our buyers are spending more, our sellers are more engaged, and the platform connecting them gets smarter every quarter." Levesque continued, "Entering the year, we said 2026 would be the year our advantages begin to compound, and we're delivering on that commitment. Given the continued strength in our supply trends and the durability of our growth, we are confidently raising our full-year outlook. We are entering the second half of the year from a position of strength, with a flywheel that is gaining real momentum." Second Quarter Highlights GMV was $617 million, an increase of 22% compared to the same period in 2025 Total Revenue was $193 million, an increase of 17% compared to the same period in 2025 Gross Profit was $143 million, an increase of $21 million compared to the same period in 2025 Gross Margin was 74.4%, an increase of 10 basis points compared to the same period in 2025 Net Loss was $(27) million or (14.1)% of total revenue, compared to $(11) million or (6.9)% of total revenue in the same period in 2025. Second Quarter 2026 Net Loss includes a $(18.6) million non-cash adjustment as a result of the change in fair value of warrant liability. Adjusted EBITDA was $13.5 million or 7.0% of total revenue compared to $6.8 million or 4.1% of total revenue in the same period in 2025 GAAP basic net loss per share was $(0.23) compared to $(0.10) in the prior year period and GAAP diluted net loss per share was $(0.23) compared to $(0.13) in the prior year period Non-GAAP basic and diluted net loss attributable to common stockholders per share was $(0.01) compared to $(0.06) in the prior year period Top-line-related Metrics Trailing twelve months active buyers was 1,107,000, an increase of 11% compared to the same period in 2025 Average order value (AOV) was $659, an increase of 13% versus the same period in 2025 Q3 and Full Year 2026 Guidance Based on market conditions as of August 6, 2026, we are raising our full year guidance. Additionally, we are providing guidance for third quarter 2026 GMV, Total Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, which is a Non-GAAP financial measure. We have not reconciled forward-looking Adjusted EBITDA to net income (loss), the most directly comparable GAAP measure, because we cannot predict with reasonable certainty the ultimate outcome of certain components of such reconciliations including payroll tax expense on employee stock transactions that are not within our control, or other components that may arise, without unreasonable effort. For these reasons, we are unable to assess the probable significance of the unavailable information, which could materially impact the amount of future net income (loss). Q3 2026 Full Year 2026 GMV $610 - $620 million $2.535 - $2.565 billion Total Revenue $194 - $198 million $788 - $797 million Adjusted EBITDA $13.5 - $14.5 million $66.0 - $69.0 million W ebcast and Conference Call The RealReal will host a conference call to review the company's second quarter results beginning at approximately 2:00 p.m. Pacific Time today (5:00 p.m. Eastern Time). A live webcast of the conference call and accompanying materials will be available online at investor.therealreal.com . A replay of the webcast will be available at the same location. To access the conference please register using this link: https://the-realreal-earnings-call-q2-2026.open-exchange.net/registration . About The RealReal, Inc. The RealReal is the world's largest online marketplace for authenticated, resale luxury goods, trusted by more than 40 million members. Our full-service consignment model—offering virtual appointments, in-home pickup, drop-off, and direct shipping—enables consumers to buy and sell luxury across fashion, fine jewelry and watches, art, and home categories with ease. The company combines a rigorous, expert-led authentication process with proprietary technology, including AI and machine learning, to power optimal pricing and processing for our members and to help scale the business. By extending the life of millions of luxury goods, the company is leading a more circular economy, all the while delivering a seamless experience for buyers and sellers. Forward Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements relating to, among other things, the future performance of The RealReal that are based on the company's current expectations, forecasts and assumptions and involve risks and uncertainties. In some cases, you can identify forward-looking statements by terminology such as "may," "will," "should," "could," "expect," "plan," "anticipate," "target," "contemplate," "project," "believe," "estimate," "predict," "intend," "potential," "continue," "ongoing" or the negative of these terms or other comparable terminology. These statements include, but are not limited to, statements about future operating and financial results, including our strategies, plans, commitments, objectives and goals, in particular in the context of the recent geopolitical events, and uncertainty surrounding macro-economic trends, financial guidance, anticipated growth in 2026, the anticipated impact of generative AI, and financial targets, goals and projections. Actual results could differ materially from those predicted or implied and reported results should not be considered as an indication of future performance. Other factors that could cause or contribute to such differences include, but are not limited to, inflation, macroeconomic uncertainty, geopolitical instability, any failure to generate a supply of consigned goods, pricing pressure on the consignment market resulting from discounting in the market for new goods, failure to efficiently and effectively operate our merchandising and fulfillment operations, labor shortages and other reasons. More information about factors that could affect the company's operating results is included under the captions "Risk Factors" and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in the company's most recent Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 and subsequent Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, copies of which may be obtained by visiting the company's Investor Relations website at https://investor.therealreal.com or the SEC's website at www.sec.gov . Undue reliance should not be placed on the forward-looking statements in this press release, which are based on information available to the company on the date hereof. The company assumes no obligation to update such statements. Non-GAAP Financial Measures To supplement our unaudited and condensed financial statements presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP"), this earnings release and the accompanying tables and the related earnings conference call contain certain non-GAAP financial measures, including Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of total revenue ("Adjusted EBITDA Margin"), free cash flow, non-GAAP net loss attributable to common stockholders, and non-GAAP net loss per share attributable to common stockholders, basic and diluted. We have provided a reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures in this earnings release. We do not, nor do we suggest that investors should, consider such non-GAAP financial measures in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. Investors should also note that non-GAAP financial measures we use may not be the same non-GAAP financial measures, and may not be calculated in the same manner, as that of other companies, including other companies in our industry. Adjusted EBITDA is a key performance measure that our management uses to assess our operating performance. Because Adjusted EBITDA facilitates internal comparisons of our historical operating performance on a more consistent basis, we use this measure as an overall assessment of our performance, to evaluate the effectiveness of our business strategies and for business planning purposes. Adjusted EBITDA may not be comparable to similarly titled metrics of other companies. We calculate Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) before interest income, interest expense, provision (benefit) for income taxes, depreciation and amortization, further adjusted to exclude stock-based compensation, employer payroll tax expense on employee stock transactions, gain on extinguishment of debt, change in fair value of warrant liabilities and certain one-time expenses. The employer payroll tax expense related to employee stock transactions are tied to the vesting or exercise of underlying equity awards and the price of our common stock at the time of vesting, which may vary from period to period independent of the operating performance of our business. Adjusted EBITDA has certain limitations as the measure excludes the impact of certain expenses that are included in our statements of operations that are necessary to run our business and should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss) or any other measure of financial performance calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP. In particular, the exclusion of certain expenses in calculating Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin facilitates operating performance comparisons on a period-to-period basis and, in the case of exclusion of the impact of stock-based compensation and the related employer payroll tax expense on employee stock transactions, excludes an item that we do not consider to be indicative of our core operating performance. Investors should, however, understand that stock-based compensation and the related employer payroll tax expense will be a significant recurring expense in our business and an important part of the compensation provided to our employees. Accordingly, we believe that Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the same manner as our management and board of directors. Free cash flow is a non-GAAP financial measure that is calculated as net cash (used in) provided by operating activities less net cash used to purchase property and equipment and capitalized proprietary software development costs. We believe free cash flow is an important indicator of our business performance, as it measures the amount of cash we generate. Accordingly, we believe that free cash flow provides useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the same manner as our management. Non-GAAP net loss per share attributable to common stockholders, basic and diluted is a non-GAAP financial measure that is calculated as GAAP net loss plus stock-based compensation expense, provision (benefit) for income taxes, payroll tax expense on employee stock transactions, gain on extinguishment of debt, change in fair value of warrant liabilities and certain one-time expenses divided by weighted average shares outstanding. We believe that making these adjustments before calculating per share amounts for all periods presented provides a more meaningful comparison between our operating results from period to period. title: Market Signals: Rates, Earnings and Private Markets
summary: Evolving Fed policy, strong corporate fundamentals and growing opportunities in private markets are influencing investment decisions for the rest of 2026.
body_text: Investment Management Market Signals: Rates, Earnings and Private Markets Aug 11, 2026 Our market signals for stocks, bonds and alternatives in the second half of 2026 indicate growth, inflation and interest rates should settle at higher levels. Key Takeaways Markets remain resilient despite uncertainty created by geopolitical tensions and volatility. A changing Fed could reshape investors’ focus from individual rate moves to the central bank’s new policy regime, with less forward guidance and structurally higher interest rates. Strong earnings—not expanding valuations—are driving stock market gains. Elevated bond yields allow fixed-income investors to be more selective, emphasizing security selection and credit fundamentals. Private equity, private credit and selected real estate sectors could benefit from improving market conditions. Despite heightened geopolitical tensions and periodic market volatility, the first half of 2026 has been a constructive period for investors. The S&P 500 gained about 10% through the end of June, while higher bond yields have improved the income and return potential in fixed income. As investors reassess portfolios and asset allocation, several themes are likely to shape markets over the remainder of the year, including the Federal Reserve's evolving policy, corporate earnings and opportunities across private markets. “The key investment question for the second half of 2026 is whether investors can adapt to a world where nominal growth, inflation and interest rates settle structurally higher,” says Jim Caron , Chief Investment Officer of Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s Portfolio Solutions Group. "That's what we're trying to understand through our asset allocation strategies, investment selection and portfolio construction." Caron joined other leaders from Morgan Stanley Investment Management on The BEAT (Bonds, Equities, Alternatives, Transition), an investing insights series, to discuss market signals across major asset classes for the rest of the year. Fixed income: Focus on a New Fed Framework For bond investors, the leadership transition at the U.S. Federal Reserve is now one of the year's defining themes. Kevin Warsh, who became Fed Chair earlier this year, has emphasized restoring price stability as the central bank's primary objective while signaling a move toward providing less forward guidance on future policy decisions. "The important debate right now is not whether the Fed cuts 25 basis points or hikes 50 basis points," says Vishal Khanduja, Portfolio Manager and Head of the Broad Markets Fixed Income Team. "It's whether we are entering a different monetary policy regime altogether. Markets may not be dealing with a committee of dots anymore, but with a stronger chair. As portfolio managers, that means placing less emphasis on predicting moves in the next meeting but more on longer term trajectory of rates." Higher yields are also creating a compelling backdrop for fixed income, with reduced probability of negative returns, Khanduja notes. "That allows us to be patient as fixed-income investors as higher starting yields and potential income can absorb more volatility and allows the focus to be on identifying the sectors and balance sheets that can consistently generate excess returns," Khanduja says. Equities: Earnings Continue to Support the Market For equities, the investment case rests on strong corporate fundamentals. In contrast to prior cycles, recent market gains have not been driven primarily by expanding valuation multiples, according to Andrew Slimmon , Head of the Applied Equity Advisors Team. Instead, earnings growth has been the key driver. "Companies are actually doing better than expected," Slimmon says. "This is a very healthy environment, fundamentally driven by strong earnings, and that gives me tremendous comfort in where the market is today." Slimmon notes that a more restrictive monetary policy could challenge that constructive environment if higher rates begin to weigh on corporate profits. He also sees opportunity among large-cap technology companies. Despite continued strong earnings, many have seen their valuation multiples decline this year as investors questioned the scale of spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure. "These are some of the smartest people in technology, and they're all saying the same thing—that they'll generate an attractive return on these investments," Slimmon says. "We're getting an opportunity to buy some very large technology companies with strong earnings at reasonable valuations." Alternatives: Broadening Sources of Return Private markets are playing a growing role in diversified portfolios. Of roughly 730,000 operating companies in the U.S., only about 4,000—or approximately 0.5%—are publicly listed. At the same time, companies are remaining private for longer, with the average age at an initial public offering now 12 years, compared with about 8 years in the 1980s and 1990s. "As a result, investors focused only on public markets can miss a meaningful portion of corporate growth," said Dennis McCabe, Managing Director and Head of Alternative Investment Distribution. "Private markets have moved from the margins of portfolio construction to the center of the conversation." The objective, McCabe says, is not to replace traditional stocks and bonds but to diversify sources of return, potentially benefiting from liquidity premiums while helping protect portfolios against inflation and market volatility. Private equity may be poised for a stronger second half as firms begin deploying dry powder into an increasingly active market. As buyers and sellers align more closely on valuations, improving deal flow and transaction activity could create a more favorable backdrop for investment opportunities and potential returns. "Higher liquidity and a boost in M&A activity are lining up to create a real tailwind for this strategy and returns overall," McCabe says. In private credit, stress in early 2026 remained concentrated in limited areas of the market. McCabe expects performance to be supported where managers maintain disciplined underwriting, strong sponsor backing and close monitoring of earnings, refinancing and credit quality. Real estate also appears to be entering a more favorable phase after several years of declining prices followed by stabilization. "Supply is down and the cost of capital has declined, but the recovery remains uneven," McCabe says. "Asset allocation is becoming increasingly important amid trends of deglobalization, reshoring and an aging population. We see attractive opportunities in logistics, industrial properties and senior living." Disclosures Risk Considerations There is no assurance that a portfolio will achieve its investment objective. title: Liquid AI Launches LFM2.5-VL-3B Multimodal Model
summary: Liquid AI releases LFM2.5-VL-3B, a compact 3-billion parameter multimodal model under the LFM1_0 license. Available August 12, 2026.
body_text: Liquid AI has expanded its model portfolio with the release of LFM2.5-VL-3B, a compact multimodal model designed to process both visual and textual inputs. Officially launched on August 12, 2026, the 3-billion parameter model represents Liquid AI's continued push into efficient, lightweight architectures capable of handling vision-language tasks. The model is released under the LFM1_0 license, positioning it as an accessible option for developers and researchers exploring multimodal AI applications. Model Architecture and Capabilities LFM2.5-VL-3B operates as a vision-language model, enabling simultaneous processing of image and text data within a unified 3-billion parameter framework. The model's compact size makes it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments where larger multimodal systems would be impractical. According to Liquid AI's release documentation, the model leverages the company's proprietary Liquid Foundation Model architecture, which emphasizes efficiency without sacrificing task performance across common vision-language benchmarks. The multimodal design allows developers to build applications requiring image understanding, visual question answering, and document analysis. The 3B parameter count positions LFM2.5-VL-3B as a mid-tier option, smaller than flagship models from major labs but significantly more capable than ultra-compact alternatives in the 1B range. Licensing and Availability Liquid AI has released LFM2.5-VL-3B under the LFM1_0 license, a permissive framework that allows commercial use with specific attribution requirements. The license terms enable organizations to integrate the model into production systems while maintaining Liquid AI's copyright notices. This approach mirrors the licensing strategies of other emerging AI labs seeking to balance open access with intellectual property protection. Developers can access the model through Liquid AI's official channels, with weights and inference code available for immediate download. The release includes reference implementations for common vision-language tasks, reducing the integration barrier for teams without extensive multimodal experience. Competitive Landscape The LFM2.5-VL-3B release positions Liquid AI alongside other labs developing compact multimodal models. The 3-billion parameter tier has become increasingly competitive in 2026, with several organizations targeting the efficiency-capability balance that enterprise deployments demand. Liquid AI's emphasis on the Liquid Foundation Model architecture differentiates its approach from transformer-based alternatives, though comparative benchmarks against competitors have not yet been published. Key competitive factors include: Inference latency on standard hardware configurations Performance on vision-language understanding benchmarks Memory footprint during deployment License flexibility for commercial applications What This Means Liquid AI's release of LFM2.5-VL-3B signals growing momentum in the compact multimodal model segment, where efficiency requirements drive architectural innovation. The 3-billion parameter design offers developers a practical middle ground for applications requiring vision-language capabilities without the computational overhead of larger systems. As organizations continue seeking cost-effective AI solutions, models like LFM2.5-VL-3B provide viable alternatives to flagship offerings, particularly for edge deployment and resource-sensitive enterprise environments. The LFM1_0 license structure further lowers adoption barriers, enabling commercial experimentation at scale.

The scholarship program underscores KinderCare's belief that early learning creates a strong foundation for lifelong learning, achievement and opportunity. LAKE OSWEGO, Ore.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- KinderCare Learning Companies, Inc. (NYSE: KLC) (“KinderCare”), a leading provider of high-quality early childhood education and care, today announced the recipients of its 2026–27 KinderCare Learning Companies’ Kids Scholarship. KinderCare is awarding 20 former students with $5,000 scholarships to support their education at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational program. The KinderCare Kids Scholarship honors alumni of KinderCare’s programs, including KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions and The Crème School, who have demonstrated academic achievement, leadership and a commitment to serving their communities. Since its launch in 2019, KinderCare has awarded more than $700,000 in scholarships, helping former students continue building the confidence and skills they need to thrive. This year's scholarship recipients are pursuing higher education across 14 states. From Oregon and California to North Carolina, Texas and Florida, these students are pursuing studies in education, social work, engineering, law, dentistry and other in-demand fields. "Learning doesn't stop when children leave our classrooms," said Tom Wyatt, chief executive officer of KinderCare Learning Companies. "Our KinderCare Kids Scholarship reflects our commitment to supporting children and families beyond their early years. These remarkable alumni represent the lasting impact of high-quality early childhood education, and we're proud to invest in their futures.” About KinderCare Learning Companies™ KinderCare Learning Companies, Inc. (NYSE: KLC) is a leading private provider of early childhood and school-age education and care. KinderCare builds confidence for life in children and families from all backgrounds. KinderCare supports hardworking families in 42 states and the District of Columbia with differentiated flexible child care solutions through its portfolio of brands and services: KinderCare® Learning Centers: early learning programs for children six weeks to 12 years old; The Crème School®: a premium early education experience using a variety of enrichment classrooms; Champions®: before- and after-school programs in local schools, and Customized child care benefits in partnership with employers, including child care on or near the site where their parents work, as well as tuition benefits and backup care across all our programs. Headquartered in Lake Oswego, Oregon, KinderCare operates more than 2,700 early learning centers and sites. title: ReNew launches national brand campaign ‘Clean Energy Humse Hai’ with Kaun Banega Crorepati Season 18
summary: ·       Clean Energy Humse Hai’ marks ReNew’s 15-year journey and celebrates the people powering India’s cl...
body_text: · Clean Energy Humse Hai’ marks ReNew’s 15-year journey and celebrates the people powering India’s clean energy future · Collaboration with Sony Pictures Networks India will bring the campaign to life through Kaun Banega Crorepati season 18 Gurugram, India | 10 August 2026: ReNew, India’s leading decarbonization company, today unveiled its new national brand campaign, ‘Clean Energy Humse Hai’, celebrating India’s clean energy transformation, the collective effort of millions of Indians powering this, and ReNew’s role in it. As part of the launch, ReNew has partnered with Sony Pictures Networks India (SPNI) to bring the campaign to life through Kaun Banega Crorepati (KBC 18), one of India’s most-watched and trusted entertainment game show. Rolling out across print, television, connected TV, digital, outdoor and social media, the campaign marks ReNew’s 15-year journey alongside India’s evolving clean energy story. It also signals the company’s next chapter as it expands beyond pureplay power production into the B2C space via its solar manufacturing business. Since inception, ReNew has played a pioneering role in advancing India’s clean energy transition. From a 25.2 MW wind project in Jasdan, Gujarat, in 2012, the company has scaled its operations to ~20 GW across 10 states, becoming one of the largest renewable energy companies in the country. Going beyond solar, wind, and battery storage, it is playing a leading role in strengthening and backward integrating India’s solar value chain with ~9 GW of solar manufacturing capacity. The campaign showcases ReNew’s several industry milestones, including becoming India’s first renewable energy company to cross 1GW, 2GW and 5GW of installed capacity. Today, the company generates nearly 8% of India’s renewable energy, enough to power more than 21 million households annually. Through its CSR initiatives, ReNew has also positively impacted over 1.95 million lives. The campaign captures this journey from the lens of the people who are benefitting from India’s clean energy transition. The campaign film celebrates India’s visible transformation as clean energy reshapes the way India lives, works and grows. Set to an evocative rendition of “ Sabke Hisse Dhoop Ka Tukda, Khil Gaya Mere Desh Ka Mukhda ,” the it reinforces the idea that the benefits of clean energy belong to everyone and that India’s progress is powered by collective action. As Associate Partner on Kaun Banega Crorepati Season 18, ReNew will help reduce KBC’s carbon emissions through renewable energy, reflecting the campaign’s clean energy commitment on one of India’s biggest entertainment platforms. Additionally, as part of a special sustainable makeover initiative, ReNew will install solar panels at the homes of select contestants, which will be later showcased over the course of the show. Vaishali Nigam Sinha, Co-Founder and Chief Sustainability Officer, ReNew, said: “ For fifteen years, ReNew has had the privilege of partnering in India’s clean energy journey. ‘Clean Energy Humse Hai’ reflects our belief that this transformation belongs to every Indian and that each of us has a role to play in building a cleaner, greener and more prosperous future .” Gaurav Banerjee, Managing Director & CEO, Sony Pictures Networks India (SPNI), said: ”We believe the most meaningful partnerships are those that combine purpose with powerful storytelling. Kaun Banega Crorepati reaches millions of homes across the country, making it a perfect platform to spotlight the importance of clean energy. Our collaboration with ReNew on 'Clean Energy Humse Hai' contributes to a campaign that celebrates India's progress towards a more sustainable future." Campaign Details: Campaign: Clean Energy Humse Hai Creative Thought: Badal Raha Hai Desh Ka Mukhda Creative Agency: Saatchi & Saatchi India Broadcast Collaboration: Sony Entertainment Television, via Kaun Banega Crorepati (KBC) Platforms: Television, Connected TV, Digital, Outdoor and Social Media Languages: Hindi, English and regional adaptations Launch: August 2026 About ReNew ReNew is a leading decarbonization solutions company listed on Nasdaq (Nasdaq: RNW, RNWWW). ReNew’s clean energy portfolio of 20.2 GW (including 1.7 GW/6.2 GWh of BESS) on a gross basis as of May 18, 2026, is one of the largest globally. In addition to being a major independent power producer in India, we provide end-to-end solutions in a just and inclusive manner in the areas of clean energy, value-added energy offerings through digitalization, storage, and carbon markets that are increasingly integral to addressing climate change. In addition, ReNew has 6.4 GW of solar module and 2.5 GW of solar cell manufacturing capacities and is expanding its solar cells manufacturing capacity by another 4 GW, which is expected to be operational by December 2026. For more information, visit www.renew.com and follow us on LinkedIn , Facebook , X , and Instagram Press Enquiries | ReNew | pr@renew.com About Sony Pictures Networks India Private Limited (formerly known as Culver Max Entertainment Private Limited): Sony Pictures Networks India Private Limited (SPNI) is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, Japan. A leading media and entertainment conglomerate, SPNI comprises 29 Premium Channels in both SD and HD formats, including leading Hindi General Entertainment Television Channels - Sony Entertainment Television; Sony SAB and Sony PAL; Marathi General Entertainment Channel - Sony Marathi; Bangla General Entertainment Channel - Sony AATH; Hindi Movie Channels - Sony MAX, Sony MAX 1, Sony MAX 2 and Sony WAH; renowned destination for sports fans - Sony Sports Network comprising Sony Sports Ten 1, Sony Sports Ten 2, Sony Sports Ten 3, Sony Sports Ten 4, Sony Sports Ten 5; Kids Entertainment Channel - Sony YAY!; English Movie Channel - Sony PIX; Factual Entertainment Channel - Sony BBC Earth; Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television (FAST) channel in the US and Canada – Sony KAL; Digital entertainment OTT platform - Sony LIV and the independent production venture for original content and IPs for TV and digital media - Studio NEXT. This Network reaches out to over 700 million viewers in India and is available in over 150 countries. Recognised as an employer of choice within and outside the media industry, SPNI is a recipient of several awards, including India’s Best Companies to Work For 2021 by the Great Place to Work® Institute, India, Exemplars of Inclusion in AVTAR & Seramount’s Most Inclusive Companies Index 2024 and listed as one of the 100 Best Companies for Women in India for eight consecutive years by AVTAR & Seramount. body_text: First Lady Melania Trump announces that another child separated from their family during the Russia-Ukraine war has been reunited with their loved ones. The ongoing Russia-Ukraine war has separated countless families, leaving children among those most vulnerable to the conflict's devastating consequences. In a recent announcement, First Lady Melania Trump said that another child who had been separated from their family during the war has been reunited with their loved ones. The announcement highlights the continuing international efforts to locate children separated from their parents and relatives during the conflict. Family reunification has become one of the most sensitive humanitarian issues arising from the war, particularly as governments and international organizations work to establish the whereabouts of children and help reconnect them with their families. Melania Trump Announces Another Family Reunification Melania Trump's announcement focused on the successful return of another child to their family. While individual cases can involve complex circumstances, reunification efforts generally require cooperation among governments, humanitarian organizations, families, and other parties working to verify identities and establish safe routes for children to return home. For families affected by the Russia-Ukraine war, such reunions can represent an important moment after months or even years of uncertainty. Parents and relatives who have lost contact with children have faced enormous emotional challenges while attempting to determine where their loved ones are and whether they can safely return. The First Lady's announcement draws renewed attention to these humanitarian efforts and the importance of continuing work on cases involving children separated from their families. Why Ukrainian Children Have Been Separated From Their Families The war in Ukraine has caused large-scale displacement. Millions of people have been forced to leave their homes, while fighting, occupation, evacuations and other wartime conditions have disrupted family relationships. Children can become separated from parents or other relatives during chaotic evacuations and periods of displacement. In some situations, children have been moved to different areas for safety or placed under the care of institutions or other adults. The issue became particularly controversial in areas affected by Russian occupation. Ukrainian authorities and international bodies have investigated allegations involving the transfer or relocation of children from occupied Ukrainian territories to Russia or Russian-controlled areas. Russia has disputed some Ukrainian and international characterizations of these transfers, saying that children were moved away from danger and describing its actions as humanitarian. Ukraine, meanwhile, has maintained that many children were unlawfully removed and has called for their return. Because individual cases differ, establishing what happened to each child can require extensive documentation and coordination. The Importance of Family Reunification For children affected by armed conflict, returning to parents and relatives can be an important part of rebuilding their lives. Separation can create emotional distress and uncertainty, particularly when children have spent long periods away from familiar surroundings. Family reunification is therefore about more than transportation from one location to another. Authorities and humanitarian organizations may need to confirm a child's identity, determine family relationships, assess safety concerns and coordinate travel across borders or front lines. In some cases, relatives may not know exactly where a child is located. Communication difficulties and the destruction of records can make the process even more complicated. Successful reunions can also provide families with an opportunity to begin recovering from the trauma associated with displacement and separation. International Attention on Ukrainian Children The fate of children affected by the Russia-Ukraine war has attracted significant international attention. Governments and humanitarian organizations have repeatedly emphasized the need to identify separated children and facilitate safe returns when appropriate. International law provides protections for children during armed conflict. The Convention on the Rights of the Child and other international frameworks recognize children's rights to family relationships and protection during conflict. The International Committee of the Red Cross has also played a role in tracing people separated by armed conflicts and helping families restore contact. Such work demonstrates why identifying children and maintaining reliable information about their circumstances is essential. The issue has also become part of wider diplomatic discussions between Ukraine and Russia, with the return of children frequently raised alongside other humanitarian concerns. A Significant Moment for Families For the family involved in the latest announcement, the reunion represents a deeply personal milestone. Behind the broader diplomatic and political debate are parents, children and relatives who have experienced uncertainty because of the war. Each successful reunion can offer hope to other families still searching for missing children. It also demonstrates the importance of sustained international cooperation. Melania Trump's announcement places another individual family story in the spotlight while drawing attention to the broader humanitarian challenge created by the conflict. What Happens Next? Although the return of another child is encouraging, many families continue to search for relatives separated during the war. The scale and complexity of the conflict mean that reunification efforts are likely to remain an important humanitarian priority. Authorities must continue identifying children, gathering information, communicating with families and negotiating practical arrangements for safe returns. International organizations can also help with tracing, documentation and family support. For children who have been separated from their loved ones, time remains an important factor. The longer a separation continues, the more complicated the process of rebuilding connections can become. Continued diplomatic engagement and humanitarian cooperation may therefore be essential to achieving further reunifications. The latest announcement from First Lady Melania Trump serves as a reminder that behind the statistics surrounding the Russia-Ukraine war are individual families whose lives have been dramatically altered by the conflict. Conclusion Melania Trump's announcement that another child separated from their family during the Russia-Ukraine war has been reunited with loved ones offers a moment of hope amid a devastating conflict. The case also highlights the broader humanitarian challenge of children separated from their families. While every situation is different, family tracing, identity verification, diplomatic cooperation, and safe transportation can all play important roles in successful reunification. As the war continues to affect communities across Ukraine, efforts to locate separated children and help them return to their families remain an important humanitarian priority. Each successful reunion is significant not only for the child involved but also for relatives who have spent months or years waiting for answers. Disclaimer: This article is provided for informational purposes. Details concerning individual children and family reunifications can change as official investigations and humanitarian processes develop. Readers should consult authoritative government and humanitarian sources for the latest verified information.

title: Communities and Families Need to Prepare For Major Weather Before it Strikes Toyota Invests $1 Million in American Red Cross Disaster Relief
summary: Severe weather events have increased 75% over the last five years, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). This impacts families and businesses in each community in significant ways. However, preparing for these events before they happen can […]
body_text: Severe weather events have increased 75% over the last five years, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration ( NOAA ). This impacts families and businesses in each community in significant ways. However, preparing for these events before they happen can decrease their impact and help develop more resilient communities. Starting this year, Toyota is deepening its decades-long relationship with the American Red Cross by investing $1 million to support the Annual Disaster Giving Program ( ADGP ). The combined investment from Toyota Motor North America, Gulf States Toyota, and Southeast Toyota Distributors reflects a shared focus on readiness, response, and long-term community support. “The relationship between Toyota and the American Red Cross is built on trust, shared purposes, and a shared commitment to preparedness,” said Chris Nielsen, Toyota’s executive vice president of supply chain. “We see this as an investment in the communities our team members call home and throughout the U.S.” Over the next year, Toyota’s support could help provide critical resources for people affected by disasters, including: More than 10,700 nutritious meals and snacks Nearly 775 shelter stays Relief supplies for approximately 530 households Recovery services for more than 300 individuals These numbers represent the long-term, broader work the Red Cross does to help people stabilize their lives after a disaster. Preparing Before the Next Disaster The year-round support of the ADGP helps the Red Cross stay ready for disasters big and small nationwide, whenever and wherever they occur. Toyota’s support also helps the Red Cross train and deploy disaster volunteers, adding critical surge capacity when major emergencies stretch Red Cross teams. Volunteers can serve in roles including shelter operations, logistics, family reunification, health services, and recovery support, helping extend the Red Cross’s reach and faster response. Beyond financial contributions, for years Toyota has provided practical support and operational problem-solving through the Toyota Production System Support Center ( TSSC ). “Working with the American Red Cross team, we were able to identify areas for improvement and new ways to address these through a more standardized approach,” said Jamie Bonini, president of TSSC. “Our team has provided real-time feedback on how to improve the local volunteer engagement to help speed the relief to families served. We’re eager to explore more opportunities to support the Red Cross using Toyota Production System principles to help others in need.” That collaboration has helped streamline volunteer onboarding, turning a process that once took hours into one that can happen in minutes. Read about the case study online . Employee Engagement Opportunities Toyota team members have shown their support for the Red Cross through volunteer service, disaster deployments, and CPR training. Most notably, several Toyota locations host regular blood drives to support the need for blood. Team members in Indiana, Kentucky, and the headquarters in Texas host five drives a year each for their local Red Cross chapters. Hosting drives are even more critical now as the Red Cross recently declared a national blood crisis following a steep drop in donations earlier this summer. “There’s a constant need for blood donations, and our team stepped up to the challenge,” said Tim Dorren, general manager in Toyota’s accounting and finance department. “Red Cross blood drives throughout the year help ensure there is a supply on hand when the need is the greatest.” In that spirit, Toyota’s renewed support for the Red Cross is more than a donation. It is an investment in uplifting communities. And as an Annual Disaster Giving Program member, Toyota helps ensure the Red Cross is equipped to do what it does best: prepare people, provide vital relief, and support recovery when families need it most.

title: B2B Digital Lead Generation: Build a System From Search Traffic to Qualified Conversations
summary: B2B digital lead generation works when search, content, forms, lead intelligence, and revenue feedback operate as one system. Here is how to build it.
body_text: B2B Digital Lead Generation: Build a System From Search Traffic to Qualified Conversations B2B digital lead generation sounds simple on a slide. Attract the right people, offer something useful, collect their information, turn the reply into a conversation. Each verb hides a different system, owner, tool, and failure point. Traffic can be weak because the message is generic. Traffic can be strong and still mismatched. A landing page can convert one segment and confuse the next. A form can ask the wrong questions. A qualified buyer can wait hours for a reply while a slower competitor books the meeting instead. Sales can receive a name with no sense of what that person was actually trying to solve, and the lead count on the dashboard can keep climbing while the system underneath quietly leaks value. We built Surface to close that gap. It connects the search that brought a buyer in, the content they land on, the form they fill out, and the rep who follows up into one system that learns from every outcome it produces. Here is how the full path fits together. Map the actual entry points A prospective customer can reach the company through organic search, AI answers, paid search, paid social, partner referral, review sites, events, product usage, or a direct visit. Each of those carries a different kind of intent. None of them should be forced into one generic "website visitor" bucket just because they eventually hit the same form. A returning visitor from a named account behaves differently than a cold click from a paid social ad, even when both land on the same page. Our Traffic Intelligence layer is built to preserve that difference instead of erasing it, pairing session and channel data with the buyer signals already sitting in the Lead Data Layer so the site can tell a warm return visit from a first-touch stranger before either one ever reaches a form. Build demand with content that AI systems can also find Search content remains one of the most durable sources of B2B demand because it meets a buyer at the exact moment of a question. That takes more discipline than publishing a list of keyword posts. Topics need to reflect real business priority and connect to something the company can actually deliver. Build clusters, not isolated posts. We call this a five-layer system in our 2026 content marketing guide — visibility, trust, conversion, distribution, and measurement — where definitions, practical guides, comparisons, and product detail all link around one buyer problem instead of standing alone. This is where our Content & SEO Agents and AI Visibility Agents work together. One researches a topic and produces a ready-to-review content campaign in well under the time a manual brief-and-draft cycle takes. The other tracks how the brand actually shows up across AI answer engines every day, so a content team is optimizing for how buyers now search, not just how they searched three years ago. Google's May 2026 guidance on generative AI Search confirms the same point from a different angle: AI visibility still rests on crawlable pages, useful content, and evidence a system can retrieve with confidence, not on separate AI-only tricks. Paid media then extends the system: capturing high-intent search behavior, testing messages, and returning informed visitors to a page that was built for the question they asked. It should never compensate for a vague offer or a broken conversion path. Design conversion pages around the click, not the org chart A buyer arriving from a research guide needs a different page than one searching for a named solution. We make this point in our guide to landing pages and conversion : a blog earns interest, but the landing page decides whether the reader believes a conversation is worth having. The page should keep the promise that got the click — the problem, the audience, the mechanism, the proof, and one clear next step. The form has to match that promise. Our Dynamic Lead Forms adjust the questions asked based on what the visitor has already revealed, and partial-response capture saves a submission the moment someone starts typing, so a dropped session still becomes a usable record instead of nothing. Once a meeting is the right next step, Intelligent Scheduling books it without another round of "does Tuesday work." Nextiva used this combination to lift conversion by 37% and collect 70% more email addresses from the same traffic — proof that the form itself, not just the campaign feeding it, decides how much of that traffic actually turns into pipeline. Treat the form as the start of Lead Intelligence, not the finish line A form submission is a new piece of operational information, not a trophy for marketing to count and hand off. Our Lead Data Layer unifies that submission with enrichment, prior site behavior, product usage, and account context into one record. From there, Lead Agents can research and qualify a lead in seconds rather than the hours a manual SDR pass would take, scoring it against an ICP defined in plain language instead of a static point system nobody trusts. Enterprise accounts route to an AE. Existing customers route to success. Early researchers go to nurture. Our guide to lead capture and routing for B2B SaaS shows why segment, product interest, and account status all change the right answer — the rules vary by company, but the discipline should not. GovSpend stood this up across 22 territories in twelve days and saw roughly a 154% lift in effective leads from the same traffic, simply by giving the existing volume somewhere smarter to go. Juicebox used the same layer to absorb a viral traffic spike without adding headcount, saving more than 50 hours of manual routing work a week. Let the system get smarter instead of resetting each quarter Nurture earns a bad reputation because most programs amount to a reminder sequence that the company still exists. Better nurture follows the actual question a buyer left unresolved. Our System Agents draw on shared marketing context — what a buyer has already read, asked, or been told — so the next message picks up that thread instead of restarting it. Numbers Station used this closed loop to grow pipeline by 30%, with 95% of leads enriched automatically before a rep ever touched the record. Measure the stages that reveal leakage Reporting should show the entire sequence: qualified traffic, conversion, qualification, routing time, first response, meetings, and the revenue that eventually closes. Reviewed by channel and offer, that view surfaces problems a single cost-per-lead number hides — a channel with fewer conversions but stronger meetings, a form that converts well but starves sales of context, a fast campaign undone by a slow reply. Our guide to attribution and incrementality is a useful check on that report: a channel can look strong in attribution while adding little real lift, so our revenue feedback signals feed tested and modeled outcomes back into the system, not just credited ones — so the next content brief, ad variant, or routing rule starts smarter than the last one instead of from a blank template. B2B digital lead generation is not a channel decision. It is the ability to turn one useful encounter into a qualified conversation without losing the thread along the way. Build that system first. Then send more traffic into it.

title: How to Choose the Right OGI Camera: Matching Optical Gas Imaging Technology to Your Application
summary: Learn how to select the right FLIR Optical Gas Imaging (OGI) camera for methane, SF₆, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, refrigerant, and industrial gas leak detection. Discover the best OGI solutions f
body_text: Why Selecting the Right OGI Camera Matters Gas leaks present significant challenges across utilities, renewable energy facilities, industrial plants, and critical infrastructure. Whether operators are searching for methane emissions at a renewable natural gas facility, inspecting utility substations for sulfur hexafluoride (SF₆) leaks, or monitoring industrial process gases, early detection is essential for maintaining safety, environmental compliance, operational efficiency, and asset reliability. The challenge is that not all gases behave the same, and not all Optical Gas Imaging (OGI) cameras are designed to detect the same compounds. Selecting the right FLIR OGI camera can help engineers and technicians locate leaks faster, reduce product loss, and perform inspections safely from a distance without shutting down operations. Understanding OGI Applications Across Industries Optical Gas Imaging technology has become increasingly valuable because it allows inspectors to visualize otherwise invisible gas emissions in real time. Unlike traditional leak detection methods that often require close access to equipment, OGI cameras can rapidly scan large areas, inspect hard-to-reach assets, and identify leaks while systems remain operational. This capability is particularly important in utility substations, renewable natural gas facilities, oil and gas operations, industrial manufacturing sites, and contractor-led maintenance projects where safety and uptime are top priorities. For organizations primarily focused on methane, hydrocarbon, and volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, the FLIR Gx320 Optical Gas Imaging Camera provides a powerful solution. Designed specifically for hydrocarbon detection, the Gx320 delivers gas quantification analytics and high sensitivity for methane and VOC leak detection, making it well suited for natural gas infrastructure, oil and gas operations, renewable natural gas facilities, and environmental compliance programs. Its ability to help inspectors identify both the location and severity of leaks can streamline maintenance planning and support emissions reduction initiatives. How Do You Choose the Best Camera for Utility and Power Applications? Utility companies face a different challenge when maintaining high-voltage infrastructure. Many substations rely on sulfur hexafluoride (SF₆)-insulated switchgear and circuit breakers, making leak detection a critical reliability and environmental concern. The FLIR G306 Optical Gas Imaging (OGI) Camera is specifically designed for visualizing SF₆ leaks, allowing technicians to safely inspect energized equipment from a distance without disrupting operations. This makes the camera particularly valuable for utility maintenance teams, contractors, and substation asset managers responsible for maintaining grid reliability. In situations where organizations need greater flexibility across multiple gas types, the FLIR GF77 OGI Camera with Lenses offers a versatile alternative. The GF77 utilizes interchangeable spectrally filtered lenses capable of detecting methane, SF₆, ethylene, ammonia, and numerous other industrial gases. For organizations supporting a variety of inspection programs or managing multiple facility types, this flexibility can reduce the need for multiple dedicated instruments while still delivering effective leak detection capabilities. Specialized OGI Solutions for Industrial Gas Detection Industrial manufacturing and process facilities often work with gases beyond methane and SF₆. In these environments, selecting an OGI camera designed for the target gas is essential. The FLIR G343 Optical Gas Imaging Camera is engineered to visualize carbon dioxide (CO₂) leaks and is commonly used in carbon capture systems, enhanced oil recovery operations, and hydrogen-cooled power generators. Its non-contact inspection capability allows operators to identify CO₂ leaks without interrupting production or exposing personnel to unnecessary risk. Facilities working with refrigerants and hydrofluorocarbons can benefit from the FLIR G304 Optical Gas Imaging Camera which is designed for refrigerant leak detection. Early identification of refrigerant leaks can reduce environmental impact, improve system efficiency, and prevent costly operational disruptions. Likewise, the FLIR G346 Optical Gas Imaging Camera is optimized for carbon monoxide (CO) detection, helping industrial facilities improve worker safety while monitoring potentially hazardous gas releases. Why Renting OGI Cameras Makes Sense Many leak detection projects require specialized equipment for a limited duration, making renting a practical and cost-effective solution. Renting FLIR OGI cameras from Transcat | Axiom Rentals provides immediate access to industry-leading technology without the substantial upfront investment of ownership. Organizations can reduce capital expenditures while gaining access to the exact instrument needed for a specific application. Fast, reliable delivery helps keep projects on schedule, while flexible rental terms allow teams to scale up equipment usage according to inspection demands. In addition, Transcat's product selection expertise helps ensure customers choose the right OGI camera for their target gas and application. Finding the Right OGI Camera for Your Application The ideal OGI camera depends on the gas being monitored and the environment in which inspections are performed. The FLIR Gx320 excels in methane and hydrocarbon applications, the FLIR G306 addresses utility-focused SF₆ leak detection, and the FLIR GF77 offers exceptional versatility for facilities monitoring multiple gas types. For specialized industrial applications, the FLIR G343, G304, and G346 provide targeted solutions for carbon dioxide, refrigerants, and carbon monoxide detection. By matching the appropriate OGI camera to the application, engineers and technicians can improve safety, support compliance goals, reduce product loss, and maintain reliable operations across utilities, alternative energy facilities, and industrial sites. Selecting the right Optical Gas Imaging camera is about more than finding a leak. Transcat | Axiom Rentals can help you identify the right equipment for your application. title: How to Replace a Character in a Video With AI for Free
summary: Replace anyone in a video with a real person, cartoon, or anime character using Magic Hour's free AI Character Replace tool. Learn how it works, what to upload, and how to get the best results with this step by step guide.
body_text: Quick Answer AI character replacement lets you swap the main subject in a video with another person, a cartoon, an anime character, or one of Magic Hour's built in presets while preserving the original movement. Magic Hour's Character Replace tool works directly in your browser, requires no sign up to try, and includes three free generations per day, with free generations limited to 3 seconds per video. It offers two modes: Character Mode keeps the original background while replacing the subject, while Scene Mode also regenerates the background. TL;DR Visit the Magic Hour Character Replace tool. You can start without creating an account and get 3 free generations every day . Upload a source video and either upload a reference image or choose one of the ten built in preset characters. Click Generate , wait around 30 seconds to just over one minute depending on video length, then review and download your result. Free generations are limited to 3 seconds and include a watermark. Paid generations can be up to 15 seconds, with credits calculated based on video length and the features you select. Introduction Imagine watching a dance video where Peter Griffin performs every move perfectly without changing the original choreography. AI character replacement makes this possible by replacing the main subject in a video while preserving its motion and timing. In this guide, you will learn how Character Replace works, how it compares to Face Swap and Body Swap, and how to create your own videos step by step using Magic Hour. Free users can test it with clips up to 3 seconds with no sign-up needed. Character Replace Tool Comparison Tool Free Without Sign-Up Works With Cartoon/Anime Reference Replaces Full Character (Not Just Face) Works in Browser Watermark Free Magic Hour Yes Yes Yes Yes No Viggle AI No Yes No Yes No Loova AI No Yes Yes Yes No CloneViral No Yes Yes Yes No One important distinction is that Viggle AI is not a Character Replace tool . Instead of replacing someone in an existing video, Viggle animates a still image using a motion reference, making it a different workflow for different creative goals. Magic Hour's free watermark is removed on all paid plans, which also unlock commercial use and longer video lengths up to 15 seconds. Character Replace vs Face Swap vs Body Swap Tool What it replaces What stays the same Best used when Character Replace The entire subject, including face, clothing, and appearance Motion, timing, and usually the background in Character Mode Turning someone into another person, mascot, or fictional character Face Swap Face only Body, clothing, pose, and environment Creating realistic face replacements while keeping everything else unchanged Body Swap The entire body and identity Overall motion and scene Swapping two people or changing a person's complete appearance If you only want to replace a face while preserving the original body, try Face Swap Video instead. For changing an entire person while keeping the performance intact, Body Swap offers a workflow closer to Character Replace with a different generation approach. What You Can Make With Character Replace Turn yourself into a cartoon or anime character while keeping your original movements. Replace a spokesperson in an advertisement for different markets without filming a new video. Test different actors or characters in a scene before final casting. Insert a brand mascot into real footage for marketing campaigns. Replace a presenter in training videos without recreating the original recording. Transform anyone into built in characters like Deadpool, Kratos, Peter Griffin, Elmo, Walter White, or The Grinch in just a few clicks. What You Need Before You Start Before generating your first video, prepare a few simple assets to get the best results. For a free test, use a video up to 3 seconds . Paid users can generate videos up to 15 seconds , with credit usage based on the video's length and the features selected. A reference image of a real person, cartoon, anime character, or one of Magic Hour's 10 built in preset characters . A modern browser such as Chrome, Edge, or Safari with a stable internet connection. If you do not have your own character image, simply choose one of the built in presets including Deadpool, Kratos, Chun-Li, Peter Griffin, Robot, Keanu Reeves, Elmo, Walter White, Stormtrooper, and The Grinch . How to Replace a Character in a Video With AI: Step by Step Step 1: Open Magic Hour's Character Replace Tool Go to the Magic Hour Character Replace tool in your browser. You can start creating immediately without signing up, making it one of the quickest ways to test AI character replacement. Step 2: Upload Your Source Video Upload the video you want to transform. For the best results, use footage with a clearly visible subject, steady lighting, and smooth camera movement.If you're using the free version, start with a clip up to 3 seconds . Paid users can generate videos up to 15 seconds , with the required credits depending on the video's length and selected features. Avoid videos with rapid scene changes, heavy motion blur, or extremely dark lighting, as these can make it harder for the AI to maintain a stable character throughout the clip. Step 3: Choose Your Reference Character Next, decide who or what will replace the original subject. You have two options: Upload your own reference image of a real person, cartoon, anime character, or illustrated mascot. Choose one of Magic Hour's built in preset characters, including Deadpool, Kratos, Chun-Li, Peter Griffin, Robot, Keanu Reeves, Elmo, Walter White, Stormtrooper, and The Grinch . A sharp, front facing reference image with good lighting usually produces the most consistent results. Step 4: Click Generate Once your video and reference are ready, click Generate and let Magic Hour process the clip. In our testing, generation typically took 30 seconds to just over one minute , depending on the video's length and complexity. Step 5: Review the Result When generation finishes, compare the output with your original video. Check whether: The original motion looks natural. The replacement character remains stable throughout the clip. The background stays consistent when using Character Mode . Details like hands, hair, and clothing remain believable. During our tests, the AI performed best on videos with steady movement and consistent lighting. Step 6: Download or Create More Variations If you're happy with the result, download your video. Free generations include a watermark, while paid plans unlock commercial usage and additional features. One of the easiest ways to experiment is by keeping the same source video and simply changing the reference character. This lets you quickly generate multiple versions without uploading the video again, making it easy to compare different characters for social media, marketing, or creative projects. Tips for the Best Results After testing Magic Hour's Character Replace tool, these practices consistently produced better outputs: Use a front facing subject with consistent lighting whenever possible. For a quick free test, use a clip up to 3 seconds . For longer projects, paid generations support videos up to 15 seconds , with credit usage increasing based on video length and selected features. Choose a sharp, high resolution reference image where the character is fully visible. Avoid rapid cuts, heavy motion blur, and very dark footage, as these can introduce flickering or character drift. Start with Character Mode when you want to preserve the original setting. In testing, Character Mode kept the background intact while preserving the subject's original motion, making it a more predictable starting point than Scene Mode. Character Mode vs Scene Mode Magic Hour includes two generation modes designed for different creative goals. Character Mode replaces only the main subject while keeping the original background and environment intact. This is the best choice when you simply want to transform a person into another character without changing the rest of the video. Scene Mode goes a step further by regenerating both the character and the surrounding environment. This makes it possible to create entirely new scenes rather than simply replacing the subject. For most beginners, Character Mode is the easiest place to start because it preserves the original setting and produces more predictable results. What to Try Next Once you've replaced your character, you can make the result even more engaging with Lip Sync , which adds realistic speech and mouth movements to your generated character. If you only want to change a person's face while keeping their original body and clothing, Face Swap Video is a better fit. For creating complete AI-generated ads with a replaced spokesperson and localized audio, Magic Hour's AI UGC Ad Generator handles the full production workflow in the same browser. Frequently Asked Questions Is Magic Hour Character Replace free? Yes. Magic Hour lets you try Character Replace with 3 free generations per day , with each free generation limited to 3 seconds and including a watermark. Paid generations can be up to 15 seconds , and the number of credits required depends on the video's length and the features you select. Commercial use is available on paid plans. How is Character Replace different from Face Swap? Character Replace changes the entire subject, including the face, hairstyle, clothing, and overall appearance, while preserving the original motion. Face Swap only replaces the face, making it the better option when you want to keep the person's body, outfit, and environment unchanged. Does it work with cartoon and anime reference images? Yes. You can upload your own cartoon, anime, or illustrated character as the reference image. Magic Hour also includes ten built in preset characters, including Peter Griffin, Elmo, Kratos, Walter White, Stormtrooper, and more, so you can start creating without preparing any assets. Does the background stay the same? In Character Mode , the original background is designed to remain intact while only the subject is replaced. Scene Mode can regenerate both the subject and the surrounding environment for a completely different look. Can I use the generated videos commercially? Commercial use is available on paid plans . Free generations are intended for testing and include a watermark. What videos produce the best results? For a free first test, use a clip up to 3 seconds . For paid generations, you can work with videos up to 15 seconds , while front-facing footage, good lighting, smooth motion, and no fast cuts generally produce more consistent results.

summary: Acquisition will significantly expand Joby’s defense business by adding a fast-growing company with established programs, classified capabilities and scaled manufacturing operations` Upon closing, Resonant will become Joby’s dedicated defense business, continuing its existing programs while expanding its portfolio to include Joby’s hybrid aircraft and autonomy technologies.
